reason: Select these 15 specialists: strassen_one_level, assembly_audit, cache_blocking, panel_packing, loop_order, b_panel_layout, za_four_tile_reuse, prefetch_locality, address_generation, sme_fp32_schedule, sme_fp32_tiles, scratch_lifetime, a_transpose, n512_fast_path, streaming_region_cost. Rank the distinct 32-row A-panel design first: its 64 KiB buffer is correctly sized for 512×32 FP32 values, and one SME region avoids repeating the measured sixteen-call wrapper. The prior panel and traversal candidates did not promote, so the reuse benefit remains unverified and the altered compute and store path needs careful correctness checks. Next, the Strassen first-store change removes a C zero-fill pass while retaining the measured wrapper’s costly seven products and packing; it is a bounded test, not evidence the algorithm will recover. The single-allocation and vector-pack changes target overhead within that same rejected wrapper, but their benefit is uncertain. A Strassen single-product-buffer schedule may reduce workspace. The loop-control rewrite has little expected effect without evidence loop control is limiting. Tail splitting targets fallback shapes rather than the fixed n=512 timing. Transpose fusion ranks last because it rereads A sixteen times and adds substantial transpose work.
